### Week 4: Lab 1 & Guest Lecture (Feb 2-4)

*Instructor traveling — Unit 1 concludes, Unit 2 begins*

| Session | Date | Topic | Format |
|---------|------|-------|--------|
| 7 | Mon Feb 2 | Lab 1: Experimental Design & Power (ungraded in-class activity) | Async |
| 8 | Wed Feb 4 | **Guest Lecture:** Yunwei Chen (Stanford) (Session 2.0) | [Remote](https://zoom.us/j/93346316978) |

**Session 7 (Async Lab):** Code-along lab on power analysis by simulation using DeclareDesign. Applies MIDA framework, blocking vs. simple randomization, MDE calculations, and Lin (2013) regression adjustment. *Ungraded in-class activity — complete at your own pace.*

**Session 8 (Guest Lecture):** Introduction to ML for causal inference from an applied health economics perspective. Bridge to Unit 2.

### Week 5: ML Foundations for Causal Inference (Feb 9-11)

| Session | Date | Topic | Format |
|---------|------|-------|--------|
| — | Mon Feb 9 | **NO CLASS — Well-Being Day** | — |
| 9 | Wed Feb 11 | ML Foundations for Causal Inference (Session 2.1) | In-Person |

**Due:** Problem Set 1 (February 11 at 11:15am)

**Preparation (Required):**
- Watch: Jann Spiess videos (~90 min total)
  - [Applied ML: An Introduction](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G5qrBvOmzes)
  - [Applied ML: Secret Sauce](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qs6JmdNoT-Y)
  - [Applied ML: Prediction vs Estimation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e2Nmlk0cbrY)
- Read: ISLR Chapters 2 (Statistical Learning), 5 (Cross-Validation)

**Key Concepts:** Prediction vs. causal estimation (Y-hard vs. β-hard), bias-variance tradeoff, cross-validation, regularization (Lasso/Ridge), tree-based methods, ML as nuisance estimation
